steps.text: Bring the rice, pineapple juice, water, pineapple, butter, lime zest, and salt to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, and the liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes. Stir in the cilantro, green onions, and lime juice to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pineapple-Lime Rice
raw_recipe.description: Crushed pineapple and lime zest make this side dish something special.
raw_recipe.name: Pineapple-Lime Rice

recipeInstructions.text: Bring the rice, pineapple juice, water, pineapple, butter, lime zest, and salt to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, and the liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes. Stir in the cilantro, green onions, and lime juice to serve.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! It's got a wonderful citrus flavor that's great with a citrus grilled chicken. I left out the cilatro (personal preference). Overall, a very tasty side dish.

I pulsed fresh pineapple in the mini chopper for the crushed pineapple. I wanted a strong lime flavor, so I added additional lime juice and zest. The pineapple, lime, and cilantro flavors all complement each other giving you a really fresh flavor. Nice change from plain white rice with minimal effort. ••••• UPDATE 4.11.17 •••••This rice always goes well with Asian dishes, and today that recipe was Thai Meatballs in a Tomato Coconut Curry Sauce (this recipe is also on this site).

07.29.17 ~ A very flavorful rice to serve with pork. I did make two adjustments since I was making this early and going to reheat at dinner time. I doubled the recipe using 2 cups of water and 2 cups of pineapple juice. I also finely chopped a fresh pineapple in place of canned and threw in some diced orange pepper that was in the fridge. I waited until I reheated it to add the lime juice, cilantro and green onions. Served this with 'Grilled Pork Tenderloin' from AR. Took this meal to my parents and everyone really their dinner.

Great flavors but it can do without the butter. I scaled down to 1/2 t, but it was still too much. It weighed down the rice. 
I used brown rice in a rice cooker and the correct amount of fluid, 1:2 ratio of pineapple juice to water. That worked. The pineapple on the bottom of the pan turned brown, I discarded that part. 
Yum!
I'm looking forward to paring this w/grilled shrimp.

I agree w/ the "needs more kick" comment... I added a diced serrano and half of a diced spicy sausage. With a very delicately flavored main dish, this might stand on its own. Also, living in a dry climate, I felt the rice absorbed all the liquid before it fully cooked-- I tried an add'l 1/2c juice and 1/2c water the next time, with much better consistency of the rice.

My husband said this was the best rice he's ever had. I found it a bit flat--it needed something to balance the sweet. I added Sriracha and soy sauce and we had it with teriyaki salmon and shrimp. Overall delicious. 
I used instant rice which just requires one cup of liquid so I did 1/2 cup pineapple juice (which I squeezed from the can of crushed pineapple) and 1/2 cup water. Very tasty and a welcome variety in our menu line-up.

Delish!! 
I had my suuuuperpicky Mr.Friend try it prior to adding cilantro/lime juice/green onion - he *loved* it at that point (as did I i) so we just stopped right there.
Used fresh pineapple and Trader Joe's jasmine rice.
Served as a complement to bbq pork loin.
Making another batch as I type

I made this as a side for Giada's sweet and spicy chicken, which has a pineapple-based, teriyaki-style marinade/sauce. I followed the recommendations of other reviewers to increase the amount of lime zest/juice, which was the perfect foil to the sweet chicken dish. 
I also used chicken broth instead of water for added flavor. Hubby wasn't a huge fan, I loved it.

I made this rice to go with baked jerk chicken and it was amazing! I followed the recipe with one omission (accidental) and one addition. I forgot to put in the salt and added a diced orange bell pepper. This was incredible! I loved the fresh, savory sweetness of it and will absolutely make it again! To address the issue of the rice burning, you need to add more liquid from the beginning. White rice needs twice as much water to cook properly. For this recipe I used 1 cup water and 1 cup of pineapple juice. That should keep your rice tender and moist
Delicious and easy. I used minute rice for a quick side dish on a weekday.

I was unsure of the flavor combo for this recipe but it was really good! Loved the subtle hint of lime and cilantro with the pineapple. Nothing is overpowering. I omitted the green onion because I didn't have any on hand. I made this in my rice cooker and the only thing I would change is to reduce the amount of water to 1/2 cup (same should apply if you make this on the stove). I didn't care for the sticky/mushy rice. Served as a side to grilled pork chops seasoned with Jamaican Jerk Dry Rub. Will make this recipe again with 1:1 ratio rice to liquid. Thanks for the recipe!

Followed the recipe, and it tasted ok. Made it with a Shoyu Chicken recipe found here. By itself, the rice was ehhhhhh. But with the chicken it was absolutely perfect. Will honestly probably make it again when I make the chicken.

Tired of the same old mexican/spanish take on rice for my burrito, I chose this. Wrapped in a flour tortilla, with shredded adobo chicken breast, queso quesadilla cheese, and refried black beans/green chilis/corn. I can't seem to make the same recipe twice without tweaking, but this rice dish is perfect as is!
This was a huge hit with my family. I paired this recipe with mango salsa cod recipe and it was the perfect combo. I will definitely be making this again.
Really good. Not sweet like it sounded. I prepared according to recipe.
Really good with Hawaiian flavored chicken
This was super light and added a refreshing pop of relief to a heavy Tex-mex meal. Loved it.

It's a good start but I'm going to have to modify it next time. It was too sour and not enough pineapple flavor. I think cutting the lime juice in half is a good idea and use more pineapple juice and less water.
